questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Weather and language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had an supervisor at USYD that helped me with all issues regarding the university. When it came to actually living in Sydney (phone, bank, transport etc.), I had to find that information for myself

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: USYD staff helped with university and accommodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that a got a room at QMB which was the cheapest option, even though it costed around 7000-8000 DKK monthly. There is a big housing crisis in Sydney so a recommend applying through USYD

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: QMB is the best and cheapest USYD renter. Get use to walk. Sydney is so much bigger than Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything gets send to you by mail and you know the deadlines in good time. The staff at USYD made it an easy proces

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Academic help, mental health help (they take it very seriously), financial help if you're struggling - they have it all

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unsuccesful. The law classes were limited and not that great. I didn't get 2/4 of the classes I applied for and it was my responsibility if my classes clashed

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you study law, apply for easy classes and avoid pen and paper exams

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The leve of course was not hard, but it is hard for a law student that comes from a civil law background. The USYD law faculty does not provide you with introduction to the Australian legal system and the teachers does not care to help.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: USYD have a very "American high school" way of treating their students. You must attend all classes and write a lot of assignments. You also have mid semester tests. They demand a lot from you during the whole semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Commercial Transaction- I recommend it if you like contract law in practice 

Conflict of Law - entirely useless for Danish/EU law students 

Rule of law and its value - it is basically legal philosophy/sociology 

Law and Technology - really interesting class and great teachers. So relevant with all the AI/GDPR/privacy debates

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Commercial Transaction- I recommend it if you like contract law in practice 

Law and Technology - really interesting class and great teachers. So relevant with all the AI/GDPR/privacy debates

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cost of living is less expensive than Denmark but rent is more expensive than Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine - I was a member in yoga society, food club society and law school society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hikes and going to cafes!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
In Sydney: Coogee to Bondi walk, Blue Mountains, Royal National Park, Spit to Manly Walk, China Town 

Go to New Zealand! It's the most spectacular nature in the world

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - it's a Western country. However be open to many cultures at USYD

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't expect to talk to Aussies. They keep to themselves

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of international students, especially from Asia. Be patient, open and understand people are different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just have fun and explore Australia! Know that you're not the only one struggling

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Phone: get a mobile plan (eSim) with Optus
Transport: Opal Concession card (you can also use you credit card to tap on the bus)
Bank: Revolut 
Food: Fishbowl, YO-CHI, Butterleaf - go to Newtown

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made and a different view on the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: USYD was not great but it was challenging

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
